en.name: Edamame, dry roasted and salted
en.summary: Salted, dry-roasted edamame out of the pod keeps 12 months in the cupboard and 6 months in the fridge. Like any roasted bean it fails by going rancid and soft rather than by growing anything, so the enemies are air, warmth and damp.
en.pantry: A sealed pack or airtight jar in a cool, dark cupboard keeps 12 months. Roasting drives the water out and salt takes care of what is left, so these are shelf-stable — but the oil in the bean is exposed to air the moment the pack is opened, and that is what sets the clock. Keep the jar closed, keep it out of the sun and away from the hob, and decant a big bag into a couple of small jars rather than opening and closing one large one all month. Softness is the first sign of age; rancidity follows.
en.fridge: Refrigerated, they keep 6 months at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. Cold slows the fats down, which is the point, but the fridge is also humid and a crisp roasted bean will go leathery in a badly sealed tub — so seal hard, and let the jar come back to room temperature before opening it so that condensation forms on the glass rather than on the beans. In a hot, humid kitchen this is worth doing; in a cool dry one the cupboard is simpler.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for roasted salted edamame. Freezing is not harmful and will hold the fats still for a long stretch, but a dry roasted snack gains little from it and picks up moisture on the way out, which costs you the crunch that is the whole point of the product. If you freeze a bulk buy, seal it airtight and open the pack only after it has fully warmed to room temperature.
spoilage: A rancid, paint-like or stale-oil smell when the jar is opened.
Beans that bend or feel soft rather than snapping.
A bitter or soapy taste even though they look fine.
Mould or clumping in a pack that has taken up moisture.
tips: Split a large bag into small airtight jars so most of it stays sealed.
Taste one before serving a jar that has been open a while — rancidity shows in the mouth first.
Keep them away from the hob; warmth is what turns the oil.
Let a refrigerated jar warm up before opening so condensation lands on the glass, not the beans.

faq.q: How long do roasted edamame keep?
faq.a: 12 months in a sealed jar in the cupboard, or 6 months refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.

faq.q: Do roasted edamame need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: No. The cupboard is fine. Refrigeration mainly helps in a hot kitchen, and the pack must be sealed hard against the damp.

faq.q: How can you tell if they have gone bad?
faq.a: Smell and taste. Rancid oil smells like old paint and tastes bitter. Soft, bendy beans are stale rather than dangerous.

zh.name: 乾烤鹽味毛豆仁
zh.summary: 去莢的乾烤鹽味毛豆仁放櫥櫃可放 12 個月，冷藏可放 6 個月。和所有烘烤過的豆子一樣，它是靠「走油、變軟」壞掉，而不是靠長菌，所以敵人是空氣、溫度和濕氣。
zh.pantry: 密封包裝或密封罐放陰涼避光的櫥櫃，可放 12 個月。烘烤把水分趕走，鹽再處理剩下的，所以它是常溫食品——但包裝一開，豆子裡的油脂就開始接觸空氣，時鐘也就從那一刻開始走。罐子要隨手蓋好，避免陽光直射、遠離爐台；大包買回來請分裝成兩三個小罐，不要整個月反覆開關同一個大罐。變軟是老化的第一個徵兆，油耗味隨後就到。
zh.fridge: 冷藏 4 °C 以下可放 6 個月。低溫讓油脂慢下來，這正是重點；但冰箱同時也很潮濕，一顆脆脆的烤豆放在沒封好的盒子裡會變得韌韌的。所以要密封確實，而且要等罐子回到室溫再打開，讓水氣凝在玻璃上而不是凝在豆子上。在濕熱的廚房，這麼做很值得；在涼爽乾燥的環境，放櫥櫃反而單純。
zh.freezer: 乾烤鹽味毛豆仁沒有公布的冷凍期限。冷凍不會有害，也確實能把油脂的變化壓住很久，但一個乾烤零食從中得到的好處有限，拿出來時又會吸到水氣，犧牲掉這個產品最重要的脆度。真要冷凍一大包，請密封到位，而且一定要等整包完全回溫才拆。
spoilage: 打開罐子聞到油耗味、油漆味或陳油味。
豆子會彎、摸起來軟，而不是清脆會斷。
外觀正常但吃起來發苦或帶肥皂味。
受潮的包裝裡出現霉點或結塊。
tips: 大包分裝成小密封罐，讓大部分維持密封狀態。
開很久的罐子先試吃一顆，油耗味在嘴裡最先現形。
遠離爐台，溫度就是讓油脂變質的原因。
冷藏過的罐子先回溫再開，水氣才會凝在玻璃上而不是豆子上。

faq.a: 密封罐放櫥櫃 12 個月，或冷藏 4 °C 以下 6 個月。
不需要，放櫥櫃就好。冷藏主要是在濕熱廚房才有意義，而且包裝一定要密封好以防受潮。
靠聞和吃。油耗味像舊油漆、入口發苦。只是變軟的話是走味，不是危險。
